title: Documents
markdown:
**What it is:** Your library of finished deliverables — memos, web pages, Word documents, spreadsheets, links to things the Executive created in your own apps, and the outputs of workflow runs — in one place.

**What it does:**

- Lists your active documents, grouped by where they came from: **From chats** first (documents the Executive drafted for you), then one group per workflow showing its two newest (**Show N more** for the rest), then **Briefs and wrap-ups**, which starts folded with the newest one showing. Click a group's heading to fold or open it.
- The Executive's own working notes (its daily look back and its market research) stay off this page.
- **Search** titles and what is inside: type a few words and the list keeps the documents that hold all of them, in the view you're on (archived ones only under **Show archived**). Every match shows, with no group folded.
- Filters by kind: **All**, **From chats** or **Workflows**, each with a count. An installed extension that keeps its own kind of document adds a filter of its own.
- Anything that isn't plain text shows a small badge on its row: *Web page*, *Word document*, *Spreadsheet*, or the app a link opens.
- Opens any document to read it. Web pages display in a locked-down frame that can't run scripts or load anything from the internet. Spreadsheets and Word documents show as a preview; download them for the full file. A link shows its summary and an **Open <app> ↗** button that opens it in the app it lives in.
- Downloads it in its own format (.md, .html, .docx, .xlsx). Any Markdown document — including every workflow output — can also be downloaded as a Word file.
- **Send it to someone**: ask the Executive to share a document with a person. It messages them the title and a link on their usual channel (the link opens in Open Executive, so it's for people who have access), or — if your email is connected (Gmail or Outlook) — emails the file itself as an attachment (Word, Excel, web page or Markdown; a Markdown document can go as Word).
- **Share by link**: for someone outside the team. **Share by link** on a row (or in its **⋯**) makes a link and copies it; anyone with the link can read that one document, with no sign-in. The row then shows **Shared by link** with **Copy** (copy the link again) and **Stop** (the link stops working at once). The link shows that version only: a revised version needs its own link. It stops while the document is archived, ends if it is deleted, and ends if the person who shared it leaves the team. A link into one of your own apps keeps that app's own sharing, so it has no **Share by link**.
- **Revise in chat**: opens a new chat about that document. The Executive rereads it, writes the new version, and archives the old one; the new version shows **Replaces an earlier version** with a link to the one it replaced.
- The Executive remembers what it has written: it can list and reread its documents, and past documents surface in its answers when relevant.
- Archive a document to tuck it away (with a quick undo) and restore it later.
- Permanently delete one when you're sure, with a confirmation step.

**Who sees what:**

- A document the Executive wrote in a conversation belongs to the person whose conversation it came from. Only they see it. Not even the principal sees a teammate's.
- A workflow output follows its run: a run someone started by hand is theirs alone; the output of a scheduled or system run is the team's, and everyone signed in sees it.
- Archiving or deleting a team document archives or deletes it for everyone.
- A document can be shared by link by the person it belongs to. A team document can be shared by the principal.

**How to use:**

1. Get something in here. Ask the Executive for a deliverable and say the format if you care — *"as a Word doc"*, *"as a spreadsheet"*, *"as a one-page web page"*, or *"in my Google Sheets / Notion / OneDrive"*. When you ask, it always publishes the result and replies with a link. For your own apps it uses whatever you've connected; with nothing connected it makes the file itself. It also drafts things unprompted when a finding is worth your time. Drafts appear as a card in **Needs you** on Home, and every workflow run adds its output here automatically.
2. Open **Work** in the sidebar and pick the **Documents** tab. Pick a filter. **Show archived** (in the **⋯** beside the filter) switches to archived documents; **Show active documents** in the same menu, or **Back to active**, switches back.
3. Click a document to read it. The page shows its format, where it came from and when it was created. A draft the Executive made on its own also shows **Why this is worth your time**.
4. Use **Copy** to copy its text, **Download** to pick a format (*As .md*, *As .docx*, and so on), or **Revise in chat** to ask for changes.
5. Each row's **⋯** menu has **Share by link** (or **Copy link** and **Stop sharing** once shared), **Archive** (an **Undo** appears for a few seconds), **Restore** in the archived view, and **Delete permanently** (you'll be asked to confirm; it removes the document everywhere and cannot be undone). The same actions are in the **⋯** on a document's own page.

**Example:** *"Put the vendor pricing comparison in a spreadsheet for me."* A spreadsheet lands in **Needs you** and in **Documents**, previewed as tables, with **Download** offering the .xlsx file. Later: *"Add a column for contract length to that pricing spreadsheet"* — the Executive rereads it, publishes the revised version, and archives the first one.

*Note: archiving is a soft-delete — nothing is lost until you explicitly delete it.*
